info.title: roadbeat Studio API — Pro — APIs & Realtime
info.description:
Self-hosted headless CMS — Content Management & Publishing API

**Pro — APIs & Realtime.** GraphQL management and delivery APIs, the API explorer, incoming/outgoing webhook extensions and WebSocket realtime tickets.

get.summary: Get the full endpoint catalog with descriptions and parameters

200.description: Every operation of the host API, generated from its OpenAPI document (sorted by path, then method). Falls back to the plugin's curated ~30-endpoint list when the host binds no document.

get.summary: Download the OpenAPI document backing the catalog

200.description: The complete OpenAPI document the CE host bound at `OPENAPI_DOCUMENT` (top-level `openapi`, `info`, `paths`, `components`, …). 404 when the host exposes none.

data.description: OpenAPI 3 document as generated by the host

get.summary: Get endpoints grouped by category

200.description: Category name → the endpoints in that category. Categories come from the first OpenAPI tag of each operation.

get.summary: Search endpoints by query

200.description: Endpoints whose path, description or category contains `q` (case-insensitive). An empty `q` returns the full catalog.

get.summary: List available endpoint categories

200.description: Distinct category names of the current catalog, sorted alphabetically.

get.summary: Get example payload for an endpoint

200.description: The curated example body for the exact `method` + `endpoint` pair, echoed back with the query values. `exampleBody` is null when nothing is curated for that pair.

post.summary: Generate a cURL command from request parameters

200.description: The generated command. Nothing is executed and no history row is written. Credential headers become shell variables so the command is safe to paste into docs or CI.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

post.summary: Execute an API request and record it in history

200.description: Captured response of the proxied call plus the id of the history row it was recorded as. The target must resolve to a path on the API host itself (400 otherwise); the request times out after 30s.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: List request history for the current user

200.description: The caller's own history page plus the unpaginated match count. `limit` is capped at 100 (default 20). History is never shared between users.

delete.summary: Clear request history (keeps saved items by default)

200.description: Rows deleted from the caller's own history. Saved rows are kept unless `keepSaved=false`.

get.summary: Get a specific history item with full request/response data

200.description: The stored request and response. 404 when the row belongs to another user or organization.
Deletion acknowledgement. Answered the same way when the id does not belong to the caller, in which case nothing was deleted.

post.summary: Replay a history item (re-execute the same request)

200.description: Result of the re-execution, recorded as a NEW history row (`historyId` differs from the replayed id). Stored credential headers are dropped and the current caller's Authorization is used instead.

put.summary: Save a history item with a name and optional tags

200.description: The row after saving (`is_saved` true, `name` and `tags` set). Saved rows survive retention purges and are what the Postman export contains.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

put.summary: Remove saved status from a history item

200.description: The row after unsaving (`is_saved` false, `name` cleared, `tags` emptied).

get.summary: Get API explorer usage statistics for the current user

200.description: Counters over the caller's own history only.

get.summary: List environments (secret VALUES are never returned)

200.description: All environments of the organization, default first then by name. Secret variables appear as names in `secretKeys` only — the values stay in the vault.

post.summary: Create an environment; secrets are vaulted

201.description: The created environment. Supplied `secrets` are stored in the per-org vault and come back as names in `secretKeys`; without a vault key (`API_EXPLORER_KEK`/`INTEGRATIONS_KEK`) the request is refused with 400.

put.summary: Update an environment; new secrets are merged into the vault

200.description: The updated environment. `secrets` are merged with the existing refs (existing keys are re-vaulted, others kept); values are never echoed back.

delete.summary: Delete an environment and revoke its vaulted secrets

200.description: Deletion acknowledgement; every vault entry of the environment is revoked first.

get.summary: Export saved requests as a Postman v2.1 collection

200.description: A Postman v2.1 collection built from up to 100 of the caller's saved requests. It is a JSON body, not a file download — credential headers are `{{variables}}` with empty values, so nothing secret travels with it.

get.summary: Get the generated GraphQL SDL schema for this organization

200.description: The SDL plus the content types it covers. A JSON body, not a file download. Requires `introspection_enabled` (403 otherwise).

get.summary: List content types with their GraphQL field mappings

200.description: The `contentTypes` summary of the generated schema — id, generated GraphQL type name and field count. Per-field mappings come from `schema/type/{contentTypeId}`.

get.summary: Get GraphQL field mappings for a specific content type

200.description: The schema summary of the content type plus its field-by-field GraphQL mapping. 404 when the id is not part of this organization's schema.

get.summary: Get raw SDL string (for external tools and IDE plugins)

200.description: The SDL wrapped in a JSON object (`{ "data": { "sdl": "…" } }`) — this is not a `.graphql` file download. Requires `introspection_enabled` (403 otherwise).

GraphQL-style outcome under the CE envelope. The handler returns `{ result, errors?, extensions? }` — no `data` key of its own — so the interceptor wraps it and the payload ends up at **`data.result`**. Execution failures and a disabled API are reported as `errors` with HTTP 200; depth/cost violations are 400 and rate-limit hits 429.

post.summary: Execute multiple GraphQL-style queries in a single request

200.description: Per-query results keyed by alias, again nested at **`data.result`** (see the single-query endpoint). A failing query yields `{ error }` for its key instead of failing the batch; more than 20 queries, a per-query depth violation or a total cost above `max_complexity` are rejected with 400.

get.summary: Resolve a content reference by ID (for linked records)

200.description: The referenced record, or null when it does not exist in the organization (or is a draft while `include_draft` is off). The record's own schema-driven fields are merged in alongside the `_`-prefixed system fields.

get.summary: Resolve an asset by ID with responsive image data

200.description: The asset plus derived `responsiveImage` data honoring the `w`, `h` and `fit` query parameters. 404 when the asset does not belong to the organization.

get.summary: List all content types available in the GraphQL schema

200.description: Backing data for the SDL `_allContentTypes` query: id, localized names and field count.

get.summary: Get GraphQL API configuration for this organization

200.description: The per-organization config row. A default row is created on first access; playground and introspection default to off when `NODE_ENV=production`.
The stored config after the patch. Request keys are camelCase (`maxDepth`, …); the response keeps the snake_case column names.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get GraphQL API usage statistics

200.description: Schema size counters plus a camelCase echo of the enforced limits. These are schema/config facts — no request counters are kept.

get.summary: List delivery tokens (never returns token material)

200.description: All delivery tokens of the organization, newest first. `token_hash` is stripped and the plaintext token is unavailable after creation — only `token_prefix` identifies a token.

post.summary: Create a delivery token — the plaintext is shown ONCE

201.description: The token row **plus the plaintext `token`** — the only time it is ever returned. Only the `read` and `read:draft` scopes are accepted (400 otherwise).

200.description: Revocation acknowledgement; every delivery request re-resolves its token, so access stops on the next call. 404 when the token is unknown or already revoked.

get.summary: List persisted queries registered for this organization

200.description: All persisted queries of the organization, newest first. Their `query_hash` is what public delivery clients execute.

post.summary: Register a persisted query; returns its hash

201.description: The registered query including its deterministic `query_hash`. Registering the same content type + operation + args again is an upsert that only refreshes `name`. Unknown operations are rejected with 400.

delete.summary: Delete a persisted query (public clients can no longer execute it)

200.description: Deletion acknowledgement. Answered the same way for an unknown id, in which case nothing was deleted.

post.summary: Execute a persisted query with a delivery token

200.description: GraphQL-shaped result. `data` holds the record for a `findOne` query (null when nothing matched) or `{ items, total }` for `findMany`; records carry the content fields plus the `_`-prefixed system fields. When the GraphQL API is disabled for the organization the handler instead returns `{ errors: [...] }`, which the envelope wraps — the errors then appear at `data.errors` and `extensions` is absent. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <delivery token>`: 401 for a missing, invalid, revoked or expired token, 404 for an unknown query hash, 400 for an undeclared variable or a depth/cost violation.

data.description: The resolved payload — a single record, `{ items, total }`, or null. Schema-driven, so its keys depend on the content type. Carries `{ errors: [...] }` instead when the API is disabled.

persisted.description: The query hash that was executed

get.summary: Get the SDL for this organization (delivery token)

200.description: The SDL for the token's organization. Returns `{ sdl, generatedAt }` under `data`, or `{ errors: [...] }` under `data` (still HTTP 200) when `introspection_enabled` is false. Requires a delivery token; 401 otherwise.

get.summary: Get realtime connection counters for the organization

200.description: Live counters from the answering instance's in-memory connection registry, scoped to the caller's organization.

get.summary: List the currently connected WebSocket clients of the organization

200.description: One entry per open socket of the caller's organization. Includes the connected user's email and the JWT expiry of the socket; a user with several tabs appears several times.

get.summary: List presence for every active content room of the organization

200.description: One entry per content room that currently has participants. Empty rooms are omitted.

get.summary: List the users currently editing one content item

200.description: Participants of this content room, with their last shared cursor and typing state. Empty array when nobody is in the room — including when the content belongs to another organization, since the lookup is org-keyed.

get.summary: Check whether a user of the organization is currently online

200.description: Online flag. Returns false for any user without a connection in the caller's organization, so cross-org presence is never disclosed.

delete.summary: Force-close all WebSocket connections of a user

200.description: Number of sockets closed. 0 when the user has none or is not in the caller's organization; clients may reconnect immediately with a still-valid token.

get.summary: Get retry configuration for a webhook

200.description: The retry configuration of the webhook. A default row is created on first access, so this never 404s for a webhook of the caller's organization.

put.summary: Update retry configuration for a webhook

200.description: The stored configuration after the patch (only supplied fields are changed).

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Preview the retry schedule for a webhook (based on current config)

200.description: One entry per retry attempt (`max_attempts - 1` entries), computed from the current config. Runtime delays additionally get ±10% jitter, so these are projections.

get.summary: List delivery log for a webhook with filtering

200.description: Delivery-log page plus the unpaginated match count. `limit` is capped at 100 (default 20).

get.summary: Get a specific delivery log entry

200.description: The delivery-log entry. An unknown id (or one from another organization) yields an empty envelope rather than a 404.

get.summary: List dead-letter / failed deliveries for a webhook

200.description: Page of this webhook's `dead_letter` deliveries plus the total DLQ count for it.

delete.summary: Purge dead-letter deliveries for a webhook

200.description: Rows deleted. Without `status` only `dead_letter` rows are purged; `olderThanDays` additionally bounds them by `created_at`.
The delivery row after the immediate re-attempt: `attempt` is reset to 1, `dlq_retry_count` incremented, and `status` reflects the new outcome.

post.summary: Retry all DLQ deliveries for a webhook

200.description: How many DLQ entries were requeued. They are picked up asynchronously by the retry processor, so no per-delivery outcome is available yet.

get.summary: List all DLQ entries across all webhooks

200.description: Org-wide `dead_letter` deliveries, most recently dead-lettered first, plus the total DLQ count.

get.summary: Get DLQ statistics across all webhooks

200.description: Aggregate dead-letter-queue counters for the organization.

get.summary: Get delivery statistics for a specific webhook

200.description: Per-status delivery counters, mean duration and success rate for this webhook.

get.summary: Get delivery statistics across all webhooks

200.description: The same counters aggregated over every webhook of the organization.

post.summary: Manually trigger processing of due retries

200.description: How many due deliveries were attempted (max 50 per call). Also sweeps up `pending` rows older than 5 minutes.

delete.summary: Purge old delivery logs (completed, failed, DLQ)

200.description: Rows deleted org-wide across `success`, `failed` and `dead_letter` older than `olderThanDays` (default 30).

get.summary: List incoming webhooks (signing secrets are masked)

200.description: All incoming webhooks of the organization, newest first. `secret` is masked to `<first4>…<last4>`.

post.summary: Create an incoming webhook — the HMAC secret is shown ONCE

201.description: The created webhook **including the full HMAC-SHA256 signing secret** — this is the show-once reveal; every later read masks it.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

get.summary: Get incoming-webhook counters for the organization

200.description: Totals, active count, aggregate trigger count and a per-action-type breakdown.

get.summary: Get one incoming webhook (signing secret is masked)

200.description: The webhook definition with `secret` masked to `<first4>…<last4>`.

The updated webhook. Note: when at least one field changed the row comes straight from `RETURNING *` and therefore carries the **full, unmasked** signing secret; an empty patch returns the masked row instead.

400.description: Validation failed — the request body does not match the documented schema (unknown properties are rejected).

delete.summary: Delete an incoming webhook (cascades its execution logs)

200.description: Deletion acknowledgement.

post.summary: Rotate the HMAC signing secret — the new value is shown ONCE

201.description: Only the new secret is returned. The previous secret stops verifying immediately, so senders must be updated before the next delivery.

get.summary: List execution logs for an incoming webhook

200.description: Execution log page, newest first (`limit` default 50, `offset` default 0). Credential headers are stored redacted; rows are purged per the retention policy.

delete.summary: Delete all execution logs of an incoming webhook

200.description: Number of execution-log rows deleted.

post.summary: Public inbound hook endpoint (no session; HMAC-SHA256 signature required)

200.description: Execution acknowledgement with the action result. Requires `x-webhook-signature`; when `x-webhook-timestamp` is sent it is part of the signed string and must be inside the replay window. Bad or missing signatures answer 401, unknown/inactive slugs 404.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (e.g. BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, NOT_FOUND)

message.description: Human-readable message; validation errors return one message per violation

path.description: Request path that produced the error

requestId.description: Correlation ID (echoes the X-Request-Id header) for support and log lookup

curlCommand.description: Ready-to-paste cURL command. Credential headers are emitted as shell variables (`$STUDIO_TOKEN`, `$STUDIO_API_KEY`, …), never literal values.

deleted.description: Always true when the row was deleted

path.description: Route path. Generated entries use the OpenAPI template form (`{id}`); the curated fallback list uses `:id`.

description.description: Operation summary (falls back to description, then to 'METHOD path')

category.description: First OpenAPI tag, or 'Other'; the curated list uses its own category names

requiresAuth.description: Whether the operation declares a security requirement

parameters.description: Path/query/header parameters, when the operation declares any

exampleBody.description: Example request body — the curated payload when one exists, otherwise synthesized from the request-body schema. Shape depends entirely on the endpoint.

is_default.description: At most one environment per organization is the default

values.description: Plain `{{variable}}` values substituted into endpoint, headers and body

secretKeys.description: Names of the secret variables only. Values live in the per-org AES-256-GCM vault and are leased server-side at execute time — they are never returned by the API.

method.description: Method echoed back from the query string

endpoint.description: Endpoint echoed back from the query string

exampleBody.description: Curated example body for this exact `METHOD path` key, or null when none is curated. Shape depends on the endpoint.

statusCode.description: HTTP status of the proxied request; null when the request never completed

responseHeaders.description: Response headers as received (not redacted in this live response)

responseBody.description: Parsed JSON body, or text for non-JSON responses (truncated past 10000 characters). Bodies over 64 KiB are replaced by a `{ _truncated, _originalBytes, _limitBytes, preview }` marker before being stored.

errorMessage.description: Transport error or timeout message; null on a completed request

historyId.description: ID of the history row this execution was recorded as

curlCommand.description: Equivalent cURL command, with credential headers replaced by shell variables

user_id.description: User who executed the request — history is readable only by its owner

endpoint.description: Endpoint as submitted, with any `{{variables}}` still unresolved

headers.description: Request headers as persisted. Credential-bearing headers (`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`, …) are stored as `«redacted»`.

body.description: Request body as sent; null for bodyless requests. Shape depends on the endpoint.

status_code.description: Response status; null when the request never completed

response_headers.description: Response headers, credential values redacted before persist

response_body.description: Stored response body, capped at 64 KiB. Dropped to null by retention for saved rows past the window.

error_message.description: Transport error message, when the request failed

name.description: Name given when the request was saved; null for unsaved rows

is_saved.description: Saved rows survive retention purges and are what the Postman export contains

items.description: The caller's own history for the requested page, newest first

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, ignoring limit/skip

type.description: JSON-Schema type from the OpenAPI document; defaults to `string`

required.description: Whether the parameter must be supplied (path params always are)

description.description: Human description; empty string when the document has none

example.description: Example value, when the document provides one

item.description: One Postman request item per saved history row (`{ name, request: { method, header, url, body? }, response: [] }`). Credential headers are replaced by `{{authToken}}`/`{{apiKey}}`/`{{cookie}}`.

variable.description: `baseUrl` plus every `{{variable}}` referenced by the exported requests

value.description: Variable value. Intentionally empty for every variable except `baseUrl` so no credential travels with the collection.

totalRequests.description: Requests the caller has executed in this organization

savedRequests.description: How many of them are saved

avgDurationMs.description: Mean round-trip time in milliseconds; null when nothing was executed

recentEndpoints.description: Up to 10 distinct endpoints from the history, ordered alphabetically

url.description: Storage path of the asset, used as its URL

blurhash.description: Blurhash from the asset metadata; null when it was never computed

colors.description: Extracted color palette from the asset metadata (entries carry at least `hex`); null when absent

responsiveImage.description: Derived responsive-image data; null when the asset has no URL

result.description: One entry per query, keyed by its `alias` (falling back to `<contentType>_<operation>`). Each value is the resolved payload, or `{ error: "…" }` when that single query failed. Null when `errors` is present.

errors.description: Present when the GraphQL API is disabled for the organization

enabled.description: Master switch; when false query execution returns an error payload

playground_enabled.description: Whether the GraphQL playground UI is offered (defaults off in production)

introspection_enabled.description: Whether schema/SDL endpoints answer (defaults off in production); when false they return 403

max_complexity.description: Maximum query cost; also bounds the total cost of a batch. 0 disables the check.

rate_limit_per_min.description: Queries per minute per organization; 0 disables rate limiting

include_draft.description: Whether Studio-session queries also see drafts. The public delivery API ignores this and uses the token scope instead.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Response-cache TTL in seconds for single queries; 0 disables caching

sdl.description: The SDL for the token's organization. Absent when introspection is disabled.

generatedAt.description: When the SDL was generated. Absent when introspection is disabled.

errors.description: Present *instead of* `sdl`/`generatedAt` when `introspection_enabled` is false for the organization — still answered with HTTP 200.

token_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the token, for identification. The token itself is stored only as a SHA-256 hash, and that hash is stripped from this response.

scopes.description: Granted scopes. 'read:draft' additionally exposes draft content.

allowed_origins.description: CORS allowlist; an empty array means no cross-origin header is ever sent

expires_at.description: Expiry; null means the token never expires

revoked_at.description: When the token was revoked; null while it is usable

last_used_at.description: Best-effort usage stamp, updated on every successful resolve

token.description: The plaintext delivery token — returned **only here**, never stored and never retrievable again. Callers send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` against `/graphql-delivery/*`.

token_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the token, for identification. The token itself is stored only as a SHA-256 hash, and that hash is stripped from this response.

scopes.description: Granted scopes. 'read:draft' additionally exposes draft content.

allowed_origins.description: CORS allowlist; an empty array means no cross-origin header is ever sent

expires_at.description: Expiry; null means the token never expires

revoked_at.description: When the token was revoked; null while it is usable

last_used_at.description: Best-effort usage stamp, updated on every successful resolve

message.example: GraphQL API is disabled for this organization

path.description: Response path the error refers to, when the resolver reports one

fieldId.description: Field id as it appears in the content-type JSON Schema

fieldType.description: Studio field type — from the form schema when present, otherwise inferred

graphqlType.description: GraphQL type the field maps to, with a trailing `!` for required fields

isRequired.description: Whether the JSON Schema lists the field as required

isArray.description: True for modular blocks and JSON-Schema arrays

referencedType.description: For reference fields, the JSON-Schema `description` (used to carry the target type); null otherwise

typeDefs.description: The complete generated SDL as one string (scalars, built-in types, RecordInterface, shared filter inputs, per-content-type object/collection/filter/orderBy types, and the Query type).

contentTypes.description: One entry per content type included in the schema

generatedAt.description: When this schema was generated (it is generated per request, never cached)

deleted.description: Always true; deleting an unknown id is a no-op

query_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of `[contentType, operation, sortedArgs]` — the id public clients execute. Deterministic, so clients can compute it offline.

args.description: The frozen argument set. A public caller may only override keys that already exist here — unknown variables are rejected with 400.

result.description: The resolved payload. For `findOne` the record itself (or null when nothing matched); for `findMany` a `{ items, total }` object. Records carry the content data with sanitized field names plus the system fields `_id`, `_modelApiKey`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt`, `_status`, `_slug`, `_locale`, `_version`, `_publishedAt`. Null when `errors` is present.

errors.description: Present when the API is disabled for the organization or the resolver threw; `result` is then null.

extensions.description: Execution metadata: `executionMs`, plus `cached: true` when the answer came from the per-org response cache (`cache_ttl_seconds`). Absent when the API is disabled.

src.description: Asset URL with the requested width/height/fit query parameters applied

srcSet.description: srcSet across the 320/640/960/1280/1920 breakpoints not exceeding 2× the width

base64.description: LQIP placeholder — the blurhash from the asset metadata, when present

bgColor.description: Background color: hex of the first extracted palette color, when present

id.description: Content-type id as stored in Studio

apiId.description: GraphQL type name generated for it (PascalCase, collision-suffixed with `_2`, `_3`, … when two ids normalize to the same name)

fieldCount.description: Number of top-level properties in the content-type JSON Schema

sdl.description: The raw SDL string, identical to `typeDefs` of the schema endpoint

enabled.description: Whether the GraphQL API is enabled for the organization

contentTypeCount.description: Content types included in the generated schema

totalFields.description: Sum of field counts across those content types

schemaGeneratedAt.description: When the schema underlying these numbers was generated

config.description: A camelCase echo of the enforced limits from the config row

revoked.description: Always true; revocation takes effect on the next request

id.description: Content-type id as stored in Studio

apiId.description: GraphQL type name generated for it (PascalCase, collision-suffixed with `_2`, `_3`, … when two ids normalize to the same name)

fieldCount.description: Number of top-level properties in the content-type JSON Schema

fields.description: Field-by-field mapping from JSON Schema to GraphQL types

status.description: Always 'ok' — a failed execution answers with an error status instead

result.description: Action-specific result: `{ action, contentId, slug }` for create_content, `{ action, contentId }` for update_content, `{ action, workflowId, status }` for trigger_workflow, `{ action, acknowledged }` for custom.

deleted.description: Execution-log rows deleted for this webhook
Always true when the webhook was deleted

slug.description: Globally unique slug; the public endpoint is `POST /hooks/{slug}`

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 signing secret, **masked** as `<first4>…<last4>` on this read path. The full value is only ever returned by create, update and regenerate-secret.

action_type.description: What the hook does when a signed request arrives

config.description: Action configuration: `contentTypeId` + `fieldMappings` for content actions, `contentIdPath` for updates, `workflowId` for workflow triggers.

is_active.description: Inactive hooks answer the public endpoint with 404

last_triggered_at.description: When the hook last executed successfully

webhook_id.description: Incoming webhook this entry belongs to

status.description: Execution outcome. 'rejected' means the signature or replay window check failed; those rows are rate-capped to 10 per webhook per minute.

source_ip.description: Caller IP (or first `x-forwarded-for` value) when it could be determined

request_headers.description: Inbound request headers. Credential-bearing headers (`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`, `x-webhook-signature`, …) are stored as `«redacted»`.

request_body.description: The inbound payload as received (third-party data; purged per retention policy)

response_body.description: Action result for successful executions; null for error/rejected rows

secret.description: The newly generated full 64-character hex HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. Shown once — the previous secret stops verifying immediately.

total.description: Incoming webhooks defined for the organization

active.description: How many of them are active

totalTriggers.description: Sum of `trigger_count` across all of them

byActionType.description: Number of webhooks per action type

slug.description: Globally unique slug; the public endpoint is `POST /hooks/{slug}`

secret.description: The **full** 64-character hex HMAC-SHA256 signing secret — not masked on this endpoint. Treat the response as credential material.

action_type.description: What the hook does when a signed request arrives

config.description: Action configuration: `contentTypeId` + `fieldMappings` for content actions, `contentIdPath` for updates, `workflowId` for workflow triggers.

is_active.description: Inactive hooks answer the public endpoint with 404

last_triggered_at.description: When the hook last executed successfully

organizationId.description: Organization of the connection (always the caller's own)

email.description: Email of the connected user, taken from the handshake JWT

name.description: Display name of the connected user

connectedAt.description: When the socket completed its handshake

tokenExpiresAt.description: Expiry of the socket's JWT as epoch milliseconds; the socket is dropped once it passes. Null when the token carried no `exp`.

contentId.description: Content item the room belongs to

disconnected.description: Sockets that were force-closed. 0 when the user had none or is not in the caller's organization.

userId.description: User present in the content room

contentId.description: Content item the presence belongs to

cursor.description: Last shared cursor position, when the client published one

typing.description: Typing indicator, when the client publishes one

joinedAt.description: When the user joined the content room

totalConnections.description: Open sockets belonging to this organization on the answering instance

activeContentRooms.description: Content rooms of this organization that currently have at least one participant

online.description: Whether the user has at least one open socket. Always false for a user with no connection in the caller's organization, so it never reveals cross-org presence.

items.description: Deliveries for the requested page, newest first

total.description: Total number of deliveries matching the filter, ignoring limit/skip

webhook_id.description: CE webhook this delivery belongs to

event.description: Event name that triggered the delivery

payload.description: Event payload that was (or will be) POSTed to the target URL

max_attempts.description: Attempt budget copied from the retry config when the delivery was created

status.description: Delivery state. 'retrying' rows carry a due `next_retry_at`; 'dead_letter' rows are in the DLQ.

status_code.description: HTTP status of the last attempt; null for network/timeout errors

response_body.description: Response body of the last attempt, as text

response_headers.description: Response headers column. Present in the row but not currently populated by the delivery service, so in practice always null.

error_message.description: Transport/timeout error of the last attempt; null when the target answered

duration_ms.description: Duration of the last attempt in milliseconds

next_retry_at.description: When the next attempt is due; only meaningful while status is 'retrying'

last_attempted_at.description: When the last attempt was made; null while the delivery has never been attempted

moved_to_dlq_at.description: When the delivery entered the dead-letter queue

dlq_retry_count.description: How often this delivery was requeued out of the DLQ (single or bulk retry)

pending.description: Deliveries created but not yet attempted

retrying.description: Deliveries waiting for their next retry

failed.description: Deliveries that exhausted their attempts with DLQ disabled

avgDurationMs.description: Mean attempt duration in milliseconds; null when nothing was ever attempted

successRate.description: Successful share of all deliveries in percent, rounded to two decimals

totalDlq.description: Dead-lettered deliveries across all webhooks of the org

webhooksWithDlq.description: Distinct webhooks with at least one DLQ entry

oldestDlqEntry.description: Oldest `moved_to_dlq_at` in the queue; null when the DLQ is empty

avgDlqRetryCount.description: Mean `dlq_retry_count` of DLQ entries, rounded to two decimals; 0 when empty

processed.description: Due deliveries that were actually attempted by this manual trigger

retried.description: DLQ entries requeued as due retries (they are attempted by the retry processor)

webhook_id.description: CE webhook this configuration belongs to (one row per webhook)

max_attempts.description: Total delivery attempts before the delivery is failed or dead-lettered (1–20)

initial_delay_ms.description: Delay before the first retry, in milliseconds (100–60000)

max_delay_ms.description: Upper bound for a single backoff delay, in milliseconds (1000–86400000)

backoff_multiplier.description: Exponential backoff factor applied per attempt (1.0–10.0)

retryable_codes.description: HTTP status codes that are retried. Network errors (no status code) are always retried.

dlq_enabled.description: When true, a delivery that exhausts its attempts becomes `dead_letter`; otherwise `failed`.

alert_on_dlq.description: Whether to email `alert_email` when a delivery is dead-lettered

alert_email.description: Recipient of DLQ alert mails; no alert is sent while this is null

auto_disable_after.description: Consecutive failures after which the CE webhook is set to `inactive`; null disables auto-disable

last_alerted_at.description: When the last DLQ alert was sent. Used to debounce alerts (`WEBHOOK_DLQ_ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MINUTES`, default 15).

attempt.description: Attempt number this entry describes (the first retry is attempt 2)

delayMs.description: Delay before this attempt, in milliseconds — the pure backoff curve without the ±10% jitter applied at runtime

scheduledAt.description: Projected wall-clock time of this attempt, assuming the first attempt is now
